title: ClinicData Liberation: productised data extraction and migration for no-export clinical software

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: End-of-life deadlines and documented migration workload (weeks of overlap, PDF-only disconnected charts) are real, but the event is one-shot rather than frequent.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Capped at 2: the only budget evidence is one vendor's published list bands (inferred budget), and the receiving vendor gives the substitute away free.

evidence_strength.rationale: Dated switch-offs, a named case study and independent migration benchmarks support the pain; the key buyer-behaviour evidence is vendor-sourced.

distribution.rationale: SEO on end-of-life queries and receiving-vendor partnerships are plausible but unvalidated, and the receiving vendor competes for the same switch.

differentiation.rationale: Capped at 2: direct incumbent overlap. ValueStreamAI sells the exact method and migration is an established services category.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A desk check plus three switcher interviews is cheap, but no test was actually run and a real pilot would need approval.

feasibility.rationale: Feasible and already demonstrated by a services vendor; per-source recipes and licence checks add real work.

economics.rationale: Capped at 2: modelled only. One-shot fixed fee against variable hours with no retention.

founder_fit.rationale: No source about who would found or sell this; null per method/scorecard.md (no source, no score).

risk.rationale: UI-level extraction of special-category clinical records has unresolved licence-term and UK data-protection exposure; risk is elevated.

economic_buyer.note: The 'documented' fees are one vendor's published list bands (inferred budget), and the receiving vendor gives the substitute away free, so a paying third-party buyer is not established.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Interview 3 recent UK switchers about what they actually paid and to whom.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Forced-action end-of-life dates plus documented migration workload (weeks of overlap; PDF-only, disconnected charts); event-driven rather than frequent.

non_paid_distribution.note: SEO and receiving-vendor referral are plausible, but the receiving vendor is also a competitor for the switch.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Test whether any receiving vendor will refer migrations and whether content reaches clinic owners without paid spend.

defensible_wedge.note: ValueStreamAI already sells the exact UI-level extraction method at published bands; receiving vendors (Nookal, Upheal) ship guided migration and give it away in onboarding; data migration services are an established category. Under method/scorecard.md a wedge that is a feature of an established category is a hard-filter failure, and a services skill is not a durable asset.

no_network_effects_needed.note: One clinic's migration delivers value without other participants.

plausible_margins.note: Fixed fee against variable hours; margin depends on recipe amortisation and there is no retention.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Price a pilot against the documented band and measure hours per migration.

acceptable_risk.note: Licence terms and UK data-protection posture for UI-level extraction of special-category clinical records are unresolved; a review-policy trigger 4 matter.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: Obtain a legal view on 2 representative source-system licences and UK data-protection before any client work.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A desk check of named systems plus three switcher interviews is cheap and decisive about whether a third party is ever paid.

not_all_optimistic.note: Buyer, wedge, margin and legal risk would all have to resolve favourably; the wedge is already contradicted and the buyer is removed by a free substitute.
